Desc_0.en: Composed by Cai Yong (132-192 CE) in the Eastern Han Dynasty, the five melodies describe five aspects of the mountains. The first is Spring Travel, telling of eastern mountains oft visited by immortals; Green Water of the ever-green waters in the south; Retired Life of the central area in which 4th century BCE political strategist Guiguzi lived in seclusion; Sit in Sadness of the high rocks in the north, upon which are monkeys and birds, watched by poets; and Autumn Thoughts of the west, where crops are watered and harvested.
Desc_0.cn: 《蔡氏五弄》由东汉蔡邕所著，共有五曲：山之东曲，常有仙人游，故作《游春》；南曲有涧，冬夏常渌，故作《渌水》；中曲乃鬼谷先生旧居，深邃岑寂，故作《幽居》；北曲高岩，猿鸟所集，感物愁坐，故作《坐愁》；西曲灌水吟秋，故作《秋思》。

Desc_1.en: Written by Xun Kuang in the Warring States period as a refutation of the Denunciation of Music by Mozi, the book is not a music score, but a thesis on the importance of music in human life. It argues that "music is to be balanced, solemn and dignified in order to ensure that the people remain peaceful and do their duties."
Desc_1.cn: 《乐论》乃战国荀子为驳墨子《非乐》而作。此论虽非曲谱，但详细论述了音乐对人心的影响，认为：“乐中平则民和而不流，乐肃庄则民齐而不乱，乐妖冶则民恶而心淫……”

Desc_2.en: Written by Cai Wenji in the late Eastern Han Dynasty, the songs are accompanied by the lamentful sound of a nomad flute and include 18 chapters, each representing a melody. The Southern Song Dynasty poet Chen Zao once wrote "You're skilled with the guqin, blessed by Cai Wenji herself. So I plead you not to play a song of farewell, or in leaving, I'll surely be moved to tears."
Desc_2.cn: “梦中曾揖蔡文姬，焦尾亲传半夜衣，莫向诗人弹别鹄，免烦衰泪对君挥”。胡笳十八拍乃汉末蔡文姬所著，因琴音融合了胡茄的哀声，且共有十八章，一章为一拍，故名“胡笳十八拍”。

Desc_3.en: Written by Duan Anjie in the Tang Dynasty. This collection of small essays provides more information on court music, dances, composers and actors, musical instruments and their uses, lyrics, plays and puppet theaters than that detailed in another collection from the period, Records of the Entertaining Performances by Cui Lingqin.
Desc_3.cn: 《乐府杂录》乃唐代段安节所著。其中详细记载了唐代乐部乐制、歌舞俳优、乐器乐曲、轶闻百戏、词调源起等驳杂内容，比之唐代《教坊记》更为周详。

Desc_4.en: The melody includes four pieces, in slow and subtle tunes. It is said to be written by Confucius (551-479 BCE) while traveling between states; comparing himself—an upstanding minister, albeit one yet to achieve true recognition—to a solitary orchid in a field of common plants. Bai Juyi (772-846 CE) once wrote: "A skilled performer played for me a moving rendition of Solitary Orchid. I realize now that playing the guqin myself can never be as calming as having others play it to me."
Desc_4.cn: “琴中古曲是幽兰，为我殷勤更弄看。欲得身心俱静好，自弹不及听人弹”。《碣石调·幽兰》共分四段，曲调清丽委婉，节奏缓慢悠扬，据传乃是孔子周游列国时，见幽谷中茂盛的芳兰与杂草为伍，触发怀才不遇之情感而谱写。

Desc_5.en: Also known as Nie Zheng Assassinates the King of Han, it tells the solemn tale of Nie Zheng (?-397 BCE), a Warring States period swordsman, who assassinated the king of Han to avenge his father. The melody is said to have been gifted to Ji Kang (223-262 CE), a renowned guqin player in the Wei-Jin period, by an ancient spirit during Ji's visit to western Henan. Years later, when falsely accused and sentenced to death, he requested that he be first permitted to perform the Guangling Folk Strains. The last to know the tune, he accepted his fate, exclaiming "Now the Guangling Folk Strains is truly lost to the world!"
Desc_5.cn: 《广陵散》又名《聂政刺韩王曲》，叙述了战国侠士聂政为父报仇的故事。相传，此曲乃魏晋琴家嵇康游玩洛西时，由一古人所赠。后来，嵇康因遭谗而被害，临刑之前索琴弹之，曲毕长叹曰：“《广陵散》于今绝矣！”

Desc_6.en: A melody composed by Emperor Xuanzong (685-762 CE) of the Tang Dynasty having dreamed of seeing goddesses in immortal realms. It represents the ultimate form of Tang song and dance, depicting a fantastic scene where goddesses come down to earth riding upon clouds and red-crowned cranes. Bai Juyi (772-846 CE) praised it, writing "All songs and dances pale in comparison to the Raiment of Rainbows and Feathers."
Desc_6.cn: “千歌万舞不可数，就中最爱霓裳舞”。《霓裳曲谱》又名《霓裳羽衣曲》，乃是唐玄宗向往神仙，幻想见到仙女而作。此曲谱乃唐歌舞之大成，演奏之时，声随风飘，或凝或散；若仙女临凡，飘然有翔云飞鹤之势。

Desc_7.en: Found among other manuscripts within the Library Cave of the Mogao Grottoes near Dunhuang, western Gansu province. They comprise 25 pieces in Pipa instrument tablature, transcribed on ancient scrolls. The obscure tablature is difficult to decipher and therefore the scores are known as the 'Scores of Enigma.'
Desc_7.cn: 《敦煌曲谱》藏于敦煌莫高窟藏经洞，仅有古人抄本流传于世。此谱乃琵琶曲谱，共分二十五段，因记谱方式古朴难识，罕有人能通晓，故有“乐曲天书”之称。

Desc_8.en: Written by Cai Yong in the Eastern Han Dynasty, this precious guide records many guqin melodies, songs, tunes, related stories and lyrics. It includes 5 melodies, 9 preludes, 12 laments and over 20 further pieces.
Desc_8.cn: 《琴操》为东汉蔡邕所撰，乃是汇集了众多琴曲、歌引、乐谱传说、词曲命意的贵重典籍。此书共有诗歌五首、九引、十二操和河间杂歌二十余首。

Desc_9.en: Written by Wang Jixin, a great Weiqi player of the Tang Dynasty. His ten proverbs advise one on how to play Weiqi: "The greedy are bound to fail. Hurry not into enemy territory. Take care of oneself when attacking the enemy. Discard a stone to gain sente. Abandon the small to save the big. When in danger, sacrifice. Make thick, powerful shapes, and avoid hasty moves. A move must respond to the opponent's. Against strong positions, play it safe. Seek draw, avoid fights in isolated or weak situations."
Desc_9.cn: 《围棋十诀》为唐代大国手王积薪所著，虽仅四十字，却道尽围棋至理。十决曰：不得贪胜、入界宜缓、攻彼顾我、弃子争先、舍小就大、逢危须弃、慎勿轻速、动须相应、彼强自保、势孤取和。

Desc_10.en: Written by Zhang Ni, a Weiqi player in the Song Dynasty, the book wisely states that "You can play also by not placing the pieces"; "Sometimes losing initiative means gaining it, and vice versa."; "Often, you begin playing close to certain pieces and end up far from them. At others you have few pieces in a given spot, yet end up with many." It's praised with the saying: "Everyone can recite the Classic of Weiqi's 13 chapters."
Desc_10.cn: 《棋经十三篇》由宋代棋手张拟所著。书中不仅有：“棋有不走之走，不下之下”；“有先而后，有后而先”；“有始少而终多者，有始近而终远者”等诸多精妙论述，更有“人皆能诵十三篇”之美誉。

Desc_11.en: Originally titled 'Weiqi Manual,' this classic was written by a Weiqi player in the Northern Zhou period and exists as a single manuscript discovered in the 'Library Cave' of the Dunhuang Mogao Grottoes. Its ancient text is hard to read, and is formed of four sections each divided into four pieces including 13 Chess Records of Han and 24 Chess Records of Wu. It Includes a variety of ancient Weiqi records that discuss intricate and unexpected strategies.
Desc_11.cn: 《敦煌棋经》原名《棋经》，藏于敦煌莫高窟藏经洞，为北周棋士所著。此经共分四部，部别四篇，有棋谱汉图一十三势，吴图二十四盘。行文古朴难懂，棋理幽玄，别出机杼。

Desc_12.en: Weiqi match records supposedly made by great Weiqi player Wang Jixin of the Tang Dynasty. He once stayed overnight at an old woman's place, and overhearing her playing blindfold Weiqi with her daughter-in-law, he was impressed by their unique strategies. Hence he recorded and compiled their matches.
Desc_12.cn: 所谓“媪妇谱”，乃是相传唐代大国手王积薪某次借宿于一老妇人家中，听得老妇人与她的媳妇夜中口头对弈，不仅妙招迭出，而且用意独特，故而暗记成谱，传为《媪妇谱》。

Desc_13.en: Written by Ban Chao in the Eastern Han Dynasty, the book is considered to be one of the most important Weiqi theses. It analyzes the rise and fall of different historic states with reference to Weiqi rules, arguing that they can be applied to governing and self-cultivation. As such, it helped to popularize the game.
Desc_13.cn: 《弈旨》乃东汉班超所著，为围棋“五赋三论”中“三论”之首。此书将各朝各代兴衰，与围棋之理相印证，认为围棋蕴含着治国之理，兼修身养性之功。此书一出，围棋兴而博道衰，可谓是围棋一道兴起的神来之笔。

Desc_14.en: Emperor Huizong (1082-1135 CE) of the Song Dynasty once wrote that "The most carefree and innocent pastime is Weiqi." Written by Li Yimin (?-? CE), a Song Dynasty Weiqi player, this great collection of essays includes four sections summarizing the essence of Weiqi manuals, compiling over 50 famous Weiqi records and various strategies.
Desc_14.cn: “忘忧清乐在枰棋”。《忘忧清乐集》为宋代棋手李逸民所著，共分四部。此书集众多棋谱、棋经之精要；兼有名家弈谱五十余图；于边角的着法、棋势等皆有录载，乃围棋典籍集大成之作也。

Desc_15.en: The poet Dou Chang (756-825 CE) once wrote, "While the eloquent will want to teach, anyone with any free time will want to play Weiqi." It is said that during the Jin Dynasty, a young man named Wang Zhi ventured deep into the mountains to chop firewood and came across a few children playing Weiqi. He was fascinated by the games, forgetting the notion of time until decades later when he found his axe handle rotted into dust. This book is a collection of the Weiqi games played by those old men.
Desc_15.cn: 有道是：“丽藻尝专席，闲情欲烂柯”。传说，晋代有一人名为王质，入到山中砍柴，看到几位童子下棋，便上前观看，岂料一眼便看了七十年，他手中斧头的木柄也早已腐烂，而那几位童子所下之棋局，便是这《烂柯谱》。

Desc_16.en: Written by an unidentified player, this manual explores the essence of Chinese chess. By outlining a variety of openings and their counter strategies, this book laid the foundation for Chinese chess in years to come, and is widely praised and quoted as an infallible manual for the game.
Desc_16.cn: 《金鹏十八变》为古代无名象棋士所著。此书奥妙无穷，衍斗炮局之变数，计屏风马之奇巧；作为象棋技法之磐基，不仅备受后来者所推崇，更被多部象棋著作所引用，乃是象棋一道之金科玉律。

Desc_17.en: Legend says this record was passed down by the goddess of Mount Li. It's said that Liu Zhongfu, a famed Song Dynasty Weiqi player, once mocked a young girl playing Weiqi alone at the foot of Mount Li. She then invited him to play, defeating him in only 120 moves, causing him to spit blood.
Desc_17.cn: 《呕血谱》乃骊山仙佬所传。传说宋代大国手刘仲甫曾在骊山脚下嗤笑摆弄棋盘的乡下少女，不料反被少女以一百二十着棋杀得大败，呕血数升。从此，这一百二十着棋便被称为《呕血谱》。

Desc_18.en: Compiled by Xu Jian (659-729 CE) in the Tang Dynasty, the book consists of 24 parts covering 313 topics. It quotes from ancient classics, pre-Tang literatures as well as poems from the early Tang, providing information to guide imperial princes in their literature studies.
Desc_18.cn: 《初学记》乃唐代徐坚所著，共分二十四部，三百一十三个子目。此书取材于群经诸子、历代诗赋及唐初诸家作品，为君王诸子作文时检查事类之用。

Desc_19.en: A widespread book, instructing children on poem composition by observing the strict patterns of level and falling tones, listing examples of perfect rhymes in verses that begin with a single syllable, developing step by step. Has topics including astronomy, geology, flowers, trees, animals, famous figures and implements.
Desc_19.cn: 《笠翁对韵》包罗天文、地理、花木、鸟兽、人物、器物等的虚实应对。从单字对到双字对，三字对、五字对、七字对到十一字对，声韵协调，琅琅上口，为稚童启蒙通识之物。

Desc_20.en: Written by Zhang Huaiguan (?-? CE) in the Tang Dynasty. A collection in three volumes with the first listing ten styles of script, describing the history of each and assessing its value. The second and third volumes are divided into three categories: 'divine,' 'extraordinary,' and 'professional.' Includes 86 calligraphers with concise biographies. An appendix adds 38 more and their details.
Desc_20.cn: 《书断列传》又称《书断》，乃是书学论著，由唐代张怀瓘所著。此书共分三卷：上卷列十类文体，各述其源流，并加赞文；中、下卷分神、妙、能三品，录古来能书者八十六人，各列小传；传中附录，又得三十八人，征引繁博，颇多佚闻。

Desc_21.en: Known also as 'Notes on Calligraphy.' Written by Zhao Gou (1107-1187 CE), better known as Emperor Gaozong of the Song Dynasty. The author shares a novel and unique interpretation of the importance of the Preface to the Poems Composed at the Orchid Pavilion, the merits of inkstones, and methods to master brush skills.
Desc_21.cn: 《翰墨志》亦称《评书》、《高宗翰墨志》，乃宋高宗赵构所著。书中对《兰亭序》之所贵、石砚之所优、学书之方法等见解皆异于时人，独到之处颇多。

Desc_22.en: Written by Cai Yong (132-192 CE) in the Eastern Han Dynasty. Via aspects such as force, momentum and restraint, it discusses calligraphy techniques including putting the brush to paper, turning of the brush, restraint in applying pressure, rounding, moving smoothly, passing lightly, adjusting speed and slowing down for horizontal and vertical strokes.
Desc_22.cn: 《九势》又作《九势八字诀》，乃东汉蔡邕所著。此书从“力”、“势”、“藏”等各方面，论述了包括“落笔、转笔、藏锋、藏头、护尾、疾势、掠笔、涩势、横鳞竖勒”九势在内的众多书法技巧。

Desc_23.en: A long poem written by an anonymous poet in the Eastern Han Dynasty. One of the most famous works collected for the Music Bureau during the Han. It depicts the tragic love story of a young man named Jiao Zhongqing and his wife Liu Lanzhi, who were forced to break up their marriage and eventually took their own lives. Chen Zuoming (1623-1674 CE), a Ming Dynasty critic, named it a "Well-written, unique literary piece that masters intricate word use. Especially in its skillful presentation of a dozen or so vivid characters."
Desc_23.cn: “长篇淋漓古致，华采纵横，所不俟言。佳处在历述十许人口中语，各各肖其声情，神化之笔也”。《孔雀东南飞》为东汉无名氏所著，乃汉乐府第一长诗。此诗叙述了刘兰芝、焦仲卿本为夫妻，却因变故不得不相离，最后双双殉情的故事。

Desc_24.en: Reputedly invented by either Zhi Yong (?-580 CE) in the Sui Dynasty, Wang Xizhi (303-361 CE) in the Jin, or Zhang Xu (685?-759? CE) in the Tang. Its principles explain how to write the eight common strokes in regular script, which can all be seen in a single character, yong. These are believed to be the basic principles of calligraphy, able to represent calligraphy itself.
Desc_24.cn: 《永字八法》乃隋代智永或东晋王羲之或唐代张旭所创。此法以“永”字的八个笔画为例，阐述正楷笔势之精要，乃书法用笔之根本法则，亦作书法本身之代称也。

Desc_25.en: An epic poem about a Tibetan cultural hero composed of some 120 volumes, and over 20 million characters in more than one million verses. Has three sections: the birth of Gesar; his expeditions against his enemies; and his return to heaven. It incorporates many fairy tales, legends, poems, and proverbs from traditional Tibetan folk literature.
Desc_25.cn: 《格萨尔王传》为藏地英雄史诗，其卷过百，诗越百万行，字逾二千万；分为：格萨尔降生；格萨尔降伏妖魔；格萨尔回返天界三部。乃藏地故事、神话、诗歌、寓言、谚语、格言等集大成者。

Desc_26.en: Confucius once said, "Only by learning poetry can you express yourself." Categorized into the 'Airs of the States,' the 'Hymns' and 'Eulogies,' the Book of Songs compiles a variety of ballads, court and Dynasty music, along with songs used in rites and sacrificial ceremonies. As one of the canonical works associated with Confucianism, it is cited by Confucius as a model of literary expression and moral behaviour for his disciples.
Desc_26.cn: 正所谓：“不学诗，无以言”。《诗经》博大精深，分别以《风》、《雅》、《颂》三个部分收录了大量的歌谣、正声雅乐、宗庙祭祀的乐歌。作为儒学要典，孔子更令其弟子们以《诗经》当作立言、立行的准则。

Desc_27.en: Written by Shen Kuo (1031-1095 CE) in the Song Dynasty, these seven-character verses on painting contain 556 words that concisely discuss and critique over 50 artists and their famous works from a unique perspective.
Desc_27.cn: 《图画歌》为宋代沈括所著，共有五百六十六字，乃是一首七言题画诗；此诗不仅语言精练，而且视角独到，论及画师五十余人，评其画作，如数家珍。

Desc_28.en: A 3-volume Song Dynasty Sichuan art history classic. Compiles great works collected by Hua Xiufu, some dating back to the Tang Dynasty. This book is organized according to the four patterns of "elegant, spirited, exquisite and vivid" and is divided into three volumes: upper, middle and lower volumes.
Desc_28.cn: 《益州名画录》乃是宋代名家黄休复潜心画艺、收集了蜀地自唐代以来众多著名画作而成的画史名著。此书按“逸、神、妙、能”四格编排，共分上、中、下三卷。

Desc_29.en: Attributed to Guo Si, son of the famous landscape painter Guo Xi (1020-1090 CE) in the Song Dynasty, this book describes in depth Guo Xi's ideas on the principles and techniques of landscape painting. It's praised by the saying "Every landscape painter will have studied the Record extensively."
Desc_29.cn: 《林泉高致集》乃宋代山水画名家郭熙之子郭思所著。此书乃郭思论其父之所思所想、作画技法而成，其中所叙无比详实，素有“未有画山水而不通读此集者”的美誉。

Desc_30.en: Painted by Han Huang (723-787 CE) in the Tang Dynasty, the five oxen portrayed are each in different postures: one grazing, one looking up, one gazing back whilst washing itself, one strolling forward, and the other using a bush to scratch an itch. With simple lines and smooth but forceful strokes, the painting is an inimitable masterpiece that perfectly combines form with spirit.
Desc_30.cn: 《五牛图》乃唐代韩滉所作。画中五牛：一俯首吃草；一翘首前仰；一回首舐舌；一缓步前行；一在荆棵蹭痒。此图之着色取相，虽皆为粗笔辣手，但久对之，图画神气溢出如生，可谓千古绝迹。

Desc_31.en: Written by Deng Chun, a collector of paintings and books in the Song Dynasty, it contains 10 volumes with 219 biographies of famous painters. It categorizes works into celestials and demons, figures, landscapes, flowers, trees, birds, livestock, houses, fruits and vegetables and other themes, discusses in detail the merits and demerits of each style, and compiles various paintings and related anecdotes.
Desc_31.cn: 《画继》为宋代藏家邓椿所著，分十卷，载有画家二百一十九人之小传。书中不仅以鬼神、人物、山水、花鸟、畜兽、屋木、蔬果、小景杂画等将各个画作分类，以细评各家优劣，还记有众多名迹、杂说、画苑轶闻等等。

Desc_32.en: Reputedly created by Gu Kaizhi (345-406 CE) in the Jin Dynasty, painted to illustrate the Admonitions of the Instructress to the Court Ladies poem by Zhang Hua (232-300 CE). Depicting 19 court ladies, the 12 scenes are completed in fine, silk-like strokes creating vivid imagery. He Liangjun (1506-1573 CE), a theorist on theatre plays in the Ming Dynasty, once praised it saying "All the ladies portrayed seem natural, as true to life as if they're about to walk out of the painting."
Desc_32.cn: “女人有三寸许长，皆有生气，似欲行者，此神而不失其自然”。《女史箴图》为晋代顾恺之依晋代张华《女史箴》一文而作，共分十二段，绘有仕女十九人。此画典丽秀润，形神兼备，如春蚕吐丝，飘飘欲仙。

Desc_33.en: Created by Yan Liben (600-673 CE), a great Tang Dynasty artist, the painting depicts the scene where Emperor Taizong of the Tang (reigned 627-649 CE) received Gar Tongtsen Yulsung (590-667 CE), Prime Minister to Songtsen Gampo (founder of the Tibetan Empire). Dugu Ji (725-777 CE) once wrote, "The two countries exchanged treasures as gifts, our people all living in peace and prosperity." It uses bright colours and smooth yet forceful strokes to present a picture harmonious yet with subtle contrasts.
Desc_33.cn: 《步辇图》为唐代名家阎立本所作。图中所绘为禄东赞朝见唐太宗之景象，正是：“金玉绮绣，间遗往来，道路相望，欢好不绝，赞普宁忘之乎”。此画设色典雅绚丽，线条流畅圆劲，构图错落富有变化，可堪绝世妙笔。

Desc_34.en: Created by Zhang Zeduan (1085-1145 CE), a well-known artist in the Song Dynasty, this priceless piece of art depicts a mass of life: 500-odd figures, 20-odd boats, 60-odd animals, 30-odd buildings, 20-odd vehicles and more. Its detail captures various walks of life in a well-balanced panorama. Li Dongyang (1447-1516 CE) wrote in the postscript, "The Northern Song capital of Bianjing is bustling with commercial activities. Crowds throughout the city gather along the river, celebrating the Qingming festival."
Desc_34.cn: “宋家汴都全盛时，万方玉帛梯航随。清明上河俗所尚，倾城仕女携童儿”。《清明上河图》乃宋代名家张择端所作。画中有人五百余，牲畜六十逾，木船超二十，房屋楼阁越三十，推车乘轿过二十。繁而不乱，长而不冗，谨小而不失全貌，可谓画中圣品。

Desc_35.en: Created by Gu Kaizhi (345-406 CE) in the Jin Dynasty, the painting is composed of three parts: Cao Zhi's (192-232 CE) encounter with the titular nymph; her departure, albeit promising to meet him again; and, knowing she was gone, Cao Zhi pining after her. It shows comprehensive brush techniques that add a sense of spontaneity and liveliness to the composition.
Desc_35.cn: 《洛神赋图》乃晋代顾恺之画作。此画分为三部：一部为曹植遇洛神之欢欣；二部为洛神之离去，两人立誓再次相遇之惆怅；三部为曹植心知佳人已去，恋恋不舍之无奈。此作意存笔先，画尽意在，轻盈流畅，六法俱全，运思精微，襟灵莫测。

Desc_36.en: Invented by Sun Bin in the Warring States period, the Golden Divination Rhymes combine the Three Styles of Chinese divination: Qimen Dunjia, Daliuren, and Taiyi. Most who study divination memorize these texts due to their simplicity and practicality.
Desc_36.cn: 《金口诀》又称《大六壬金口诀》，为战国孙膑所传。此诀融合了奇门、六壬、太乙三式之要领，又兼简单易学，易用之长，学易者多习此诀。

Desc_37.en: In five volumes, it explains the theory of the Four Pillars that uses one's birth chart (including birth year, month, day, and hour) to predict their fate based on eight categories reflecting their fortune, social status, ability and luck.
Desc_37.cn: 《渊海子平》共分五卷，乃是以八字：“财官印食杀伤枭劫”之格局将人之运命分为三六九等的奇书。此书能以人出生之年、月、日、时，论人之生克旺相、休囚制化、祸福生死，可谓应验如神。

Desc_38.en: A technique invented by the ancient goddess, the Mysterious Lady of the Nine Heavens. Considered the most important of the Three Styles of Chinese divination, it is composed of three skills that can be applied to all aspects of life. It's said that through mastering the technique, you'll know your enemy better than they do themselves.
Desc_38.cn: 《奇门遁甲》为奇门、六壬、太乙三式之首，乃九天玄女所创。此法由“奇”、“门”、“遁甲”三部奇术组成，以之算天计地，无有不准，正是：“学会奇门遁，来人不用问”。

Desc_39.en: Forbidden to all but the Imperial Emperors, this fortune-telling skill was passed down to generations of imperial astronomers, rarely used by commoners. It establishes a birth chart of the 12 Palaces, forecasting future events, with the help of the 108 Stars. Hence, one can change one's destiny by manipulating the four variables of power, fortune, fame and luck.
Desc_39.cn: 《紫微斗数》乃帝王之学，仅由历代钦天监一脉单传，罕于民间流传。此数乃是以人生十二宫之数构化命盘；辅以一百零八星预测事物吉凶；再以四化之数化转命运，从而推演人生万象之奇术。

Desc_40.en: Divided into 120 volumes, the treatise was compiled by Gautama Siddha who resided in the capital Chang'an during the Tang Dynasty. It is a collection of astronomical phenomena, star charts, calculations, different calendars and divination techniques concerning humans, spirits, implements, plants and animals.
Desc_40.cn: 《开元占经》共分一百二十卷，为世居唐代长安的印度人瞿昙悉达所著。其中既载有各类天象之记载，亦载有大量星图与算法；不仅记有历法二十九种，还有涉及草木鸟兽、人鬼器物的诸多占星之术与格物宇宙之道。

Desc_41.en: A retelling of the Warring States period classic, Master Gan's and Master Shi's Star Manual, the book discusses the divination method of observing the five visible planets (namely Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, Mars and Saturn) and their movements.
Desc_41.cn: 《五星占》即战国时期《甘石星经》之所传。乃是通过记录与观察太白、岁星、辰星、荧惑、镇星这金、木、水、火、土五星的运行与异相，从而占卜吉凶的上古奇技。

Desc_42.en: Written by Zou Yan (305-240 BCE), a philosopher of the Yin and Yang School in the Warring States period. This ingenious book is divided into 49 chapters, seven each on Heaven and Earth, Yin and Yang, the interaction of the Five Elements, the cycle of the Five Elements, the theory of Earth, astronomical phenomena, and mountains and rivers.
Desc_42.cn: 《邹子》为战国阴阳家邹衍所著，共分四十九篇：其中，七篇论昊天厚土；七篇论阴阳变化；七篇论五行生胜；七篇论五德终始；七篇论大九州说；七篇论日月星辰；七篇论山川河势。凡书中所论，句句精妙绝伦，道真洞玄。

Desc_43.en: Believed to be the origin of the theory of Yin and Yang, Five Elements, and astrology and divination. These two patterns laid the foundation for Tai Chi, the Eight Trigrams, Book of Changes, Sexagenary Cycle, Nine Planets and Fengshui. As written in the Book of Changes: "Thus, people divine by stalks and turtle shells, observing the changes in nature and motion of the planets, following the Yellow River Map and Lo Shu Square."
Desc_43.cn: “是故天生神物，圣人则之；天地变化，圣人故之；天垂象见吉凶，圣人象之；河出《图》，洛出《书》，圣人则之”。《河图洛书》为阴阳五行术数之源，卜筮一道之开端，太极、八卦、周易、六甲、九星、风水等等皆可追源至此。

Desc_44.en: Written by Ji Chang (1152-1056 BCE), King Wen of Zhou, the book contains the 'Classic' and the 'Commentary.' The Book of Changes applies to all things within heaven and earth, including astronomy, geology, music, military strategies, phonology and mathematics. Even the art of alchemy can be quoted from the Book of Changes, making it the source of all Tao.
Desc_44.cn: 《周易》为周文王姬昌所作，分为《经》、《传》两部。《易》道广大，无所不包，旁及天文、地理、乐律、兵法、韵学、算术等等，以逮方外之炉火，皆可援《易》以为说，可谓大道之源也。

Desc_45.en: Consisting of quotations from ancient writings, the book discusses the different qualities of water used for making tea. It is divided into ten chapters: Sources, Stony Creeks, Cold and Clear Waters, Sweet and Fragrant Waters, Waters Befitting to Tea, Numinous Waters, Extraordinary Spring Waters, Riverine Waters, Waters from Wells and the Epilogue.
Desc_45.cn: 《煮泉小品》共分为：源泉、石流、清寒、甘香、宜茶、灵水、异水、江水、井水、绪谈十章。乃是集前人之经验，专论茶水品质之著述。

Desc_46.en: Written by Dou Ping (?-? CE) during the Song Dynasty, the book discusses 13 topics relating to liquor: its origin; terminology; anecdotes; occasions of use; moderate drinking, self-control and the loss of; warnings; liquor in myth and legend; liquor from foreign countries; properties and tastes; liquor vessels, drinking games and an appendix.
Desc_46.cn: 《酒谱》乃宋代窦苹所著。书中论述共有一十三项：酒之源一、酒之名二、酒之事三、酒之功四、温克五、乱德六、诫失七、神异八、异域九、性味十、饮器十一、酒令十二、总论十三。

Desc_47.en: A masterpiece regarding the art of tea, this manual contains guidelines for the proper preparations of brewing tea and is derived from a chapter in Tea Classics. It defines the 16 qualities of tea brewing water and assesses the respective merits and demerits of temperature, pouring speed, as well as various utensils and firewood.
Desc_47.cn: 《十六汤品》为茶道名作，乃是对《茶经》中“煮法”一章加以衍释而成。此书根据茶水冷热程度之不同、注水缓急程度之不同、所用茶具之不同、所依薪柴之不同，而作十六汤品，分别计其得失。

Desc_48.en: Written by Wang Fu in the Tang Dynasty, the essay was discovered among the Dunhuang manuscripts. It personifies tea and liquor, depicting a discourse between them in which each argues their merits. Tea is praised as "the first of the Hundred Plants and the flower of the Ten Thousand Plants," while liquor can "comfort the dead and calm the living, and even the divine are pleased by its fragrance."
Desc_48.cn: 《茶酒论》乃敦煌遗书，由唐代王敷所著。此书拟茶酒之口各述已长，互争长短，辩诘生动有趣，譬喻深刻，赞茶为：“百草之首，万木之花”，称酒能：“和死定生，神明歆气”。

Desc_49.en: Written by Zhao Ji (1082-1135 CE), Emperor Huizong of the Song Dynasty, this 20-chapter book provides a detailed, vivid and masterful discussion on the influence of location, season and weather on tea leaves; as well as the making, competing and whisking of tea.
Desc_49.cn: 《大观茶论》共分二十篇，乃宋徽宗赵佶所著。书中于茶叶产地之阴阳相济、天时于采制之影响、烹试之技法、斗茶、点茶等皆有论解，不仅见解精辟，而且论述深刻。

Desc_50.en: Written in the Song Dynasty, the book begins with a general introduction to the origin of liquor, then describes the production of more than ten kinds of fermentation, and ends with the manufacture of different types of liquor. It is regarded as one of the most valuable sources on liquor culture for its detailed explanations and discussion.
Desc_50.cn: 《北山酒经》成书于宋代，共分上、中、下三卷：上卷乃是总论，论酒之由来；中卷载制曲法门数十种；下卷述酿酒诸法。此书论述详尽，理论精妙，可谓天下论酒书中之极品。

Desc_51.en: A treatise on water for brewing tea, written by Ouyang Xiu (1007-1072 CE) of the Song Dynasty. Incisive yet objective, it refuted Zhang Youxin's ideas in favor of Lu Yu's theory of water classification, and later became the accepted convention. It measures water quality like this: "Good water should flow rather than stagnate, so the water quality of wells that draw water frequently is better. Although the river water is constantly flowing, the water quality is messy due to the collection of water from other sources, so the water quality of the river water is not as good as mountain spring water."
Desc_51.cn: 《大明水记》乃宋代欧阳修论茶水之专文。书中驳论张又新所分二十等水品，言：“羽之论水，恶汀浸而喜泉流，故井取多汲者，江虽云流，然众水杂聚，故次于山水，惟此说近物理云。”其言精辟入理，古今往来，言其辩水论最为公允。

Desc_52.en: A classic of liquor brewing written by Su Shi (aka Su Dongpo, 1037-1101 CE) of the Song Dynasty. Concise and comprehensive, it covers most ancient liquor brewing techniques. It's said to leave the reader tipsy from just a few paragraphs.
Desc_52.cn: 《东坡酒经》由宋代苏轼所著，乃酿酒著作之经典。此书共有三百七十七字，简言蕴意，包含“制曲、用料、用曲、投料、原料出酒率、酿造”等一系列造酒古法，仅阅得二三篇章，便足以醺醺然独步千古。

Desc_53.en: The earliest and perhaps most well-known treatise on tea, written by Lu Yu (733-804 CE) of the Tang Dynasty. With its concise, refined and poetic style, it covers a variety of topics. In its three scrolls, it's split into: Origins, Rearing Tools, Production, Production Tools, Fermentation, Drinking, Affairs, Locations, Notes, and Plans.
Desc_53.cn: 《茶经》乃唐代陆羽所书，共分三卷十节。卷上：一之源；二之具；三之造；卷中：四之器；卷下：五之煮；六之饮；七之事；八之出；九之略；十之图。其论茶详实，开创一代茶道先河，若谈茶事，首推此书。

Desc_54.en: Compiled during the Spring and Autumn (770-476 BCE) and Warring States (476-221 BCE) periods, author unknown. It's the only book of the era concerning the construction of ding vessels, including bronze work, casting, and decoration.
Desc_54.cn: 《鼎书》成书于春秋战国时期，作者姓名不详，书中记述青铜器之冶炼及技巧，辅以失蜡铸造与各种装饰工艺，乃春秋时期唯一一本记录青铜冶炼之文章。

Desc_55.en: Invented by a miner during the Song Dynasty to facilitate the blasting process. Spread across the land by word of mouth, its mining techniques were then developed and compiled into this book named "The Mnemonics of Blasting."
Desc_55.cn: 宋朝年间，龙泉县一位姓刘的矿工根据火爆法采矿技法编撰出了一段口诀，后此口诀口耳相传，传至大江南北，便有时人根据此口诀完善了火爆采矿技法并编撰成书，取名为《火爆诀》。

Desc_56.en: Compiled by Tao Hongjing of the Northern and Southern dynasties. Details dozens of famous swords. Special iron-casting methods are also present; metallurgy's cutting-edge at the time. Swords forged through such methods could cut through 30 layers of armor, hence considered the most formidable weapons.
Desc_56.cn: 《古今刀剑录》乃南朝陶弘景所著，录有：诸刀剑、蜀将刀、吴将刀、魏将刀等四类共四十余件古今兵器。书中所述“灌钢”之术，乃当时铸术之最，灌钢宿铁刀可斩甲过三十扎，时人谓之神兵。

Desc_57.en: King Goujian of Yue (520-465 BCE) summoned one of his retainers, Xue Zhu, to judge 5 famous swords from his collection. Xue Zhu regarded Haocao and Juque, and said "These are no precious swords." But upon seeing Chunjun, he deemed it "More precious than a city of gold; a river of gems." This story was hence recorded as 'Xue Zhu Judges the Swords.'
Desc_57.cn: 秦人薛烛为越王勾践相看五剑，言毫曹和巨阙：“非宝剑也。”又言纯钧：“虽倾城量金，珠玉竭河，独不得此一物。”时人将此事记述成书，遂成《薛烛相剑》。

Desc_58.en: Compiled by Li Daoyuan during the Northern Wei Dynasty. Discusses the source, course, and minerals (gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, mercury, etc.) of 1,252 rivers. A vital book for smiths, as many relied on its water classifications.
Desc_58.cn: 《水经注》乃北魏郦道元所著，书中录有一千二百五十二条河流地址以及水质特性，记叙水中之矿物，如金、银、铜、铁、锡、汞等，后世铸造师多以此书区分河流水质而锻造器物，乃锻造行业不可不熟读之文章。

Desc_59.en: According to the legend, Goujian (520?-465? BCE), king of the Kingdom of Yue, once assigned artists to illustrate the five treasured swords in his possession. These five scrolls were later buried with him. They resurfaced when his tomb was robbed during the Tang Dynasty, becoming known as the 'Secret Collection of Goujian.'
Desc_59.cn: 传说，越王勾践曾命人为自己所收藏之五把宝剑绘图著述，勾践逝世以后，便以这五卷图谱作为陪葬之物。唐朝年间，勾践墓被盗，五卷图谱流出，世人便将其五卷图谱总称为《越王秘藏》。

Desc_60.en: An official book of technologies compiled during the Spring and Autumn (770-476 BCE) and Warring States (476-221 BCE) periods. Details bronze casting, carriages and weapons manufacture, a metrological standard, musical instrument construction and city planning. A comprehensive encyclopedia of its time.
Desc_60.cn: 《考工记》乃春秋战国时期之官书，分上下两卷，书中论述了攻木之工，攻金之工，攻皮之工，设色之工，刮摩之工，抟埴之工的行业规范及制造工业，乃是迄今为止，囊括百工最为俱全之书。

Desc_61.en: It's said that, in the Tang Dynasty, a Taoist discovered the book while staying the night at a run-down temple. It is an illustrated manual on the ingeniously intricate sword-smithing techniques of Ou Yezi, a legendary master swordsmith from the Spring and Autumn period.
Desc_61.cn: 唐末年间，一无名道士夜宿破观，忽闻墙壁之内有异响，遂乘夜凿壁，《欧祖遗书》乃现，此书记有欧冶子锻造神兵利器的诸多秘法与图录，无一不是鬼设神施，巧夺天工之法。

Desc_62.en: Written during the Wei, Jin, and the Southern and Northern Dynasties. This secret tome is a catalogue of Kunwu, rare jade, starting from the Spring and Autumn period, with vivid illustrations and commentaries on jade qualities. It has fascinated jade lovers for generations with its eloquence.
Desc_62.cn: 《五音集韻》有言：琨珸，美石也。《琨珸册》乃魏晋南北朝时期的一部奇书，书中论述春秋战国时期至今之绝世美玉，并绘有图画，细评玉之优缺，遣词造句侈丽宏衍，观者犹如亲见，无不心生向往。

Desc_63.en: Contains 4 chapters: Judging Wood, Felling Trees, Cutting Lumber, and Woodwork. A must-read for all carpenters, with each aspect of the trade discussed in detail.
Desc_63.cn: 《木工考》全书共分四篇十三节，一篇为论木；二篇为断木；三篇为裁木；四篇为木器。从木之选材至造成木器，皆详细叙述，若从木工之事，不可不读此书。

Desc_64.en: The East Garden was a huge mansion owned by Cai Jing (1047-1126 CE) for the cultivation of numerous exotic and rare plants. Written as a satire for his extravagant lifestyle, the book offers a detailed description of the plants grown in the garden. While a little flamboyant, it is still a valuable guide for studying the growth habits of herbs and trees.
Desc_64.cn: 所谓东园，乃蔡京置于城东，占地数十里，植有无数奇花异木的府邸，时人为讽其奢，遂编撰此书，书中详细记载了蔡京东园之百花百木，虽内容多有浮夸，但于后人了解各类草木的生长习性，仍有极大的帮助。

Desc_65.en: It is said that Yang Guang (569-618 CE), Emperor Yang of Sui, once ordered the manufacture of tens of loong boats and hundreds of luxurious carriages for his visit to Yangzhou. The book is written by the manufacturers to record the various joining and nailing techniques.
Desc_65.cn: 隋炀帝杨广为一游扬州，命官吏督造龙船数十艘，奢华马车数百辆，督造者将龙船、马车之榫接、钉合方法尽数编写成书，称为《舟车枢要》。

Desc_66.en: The earliest Chinese book on mathematics. Its 9 chapters cover 246 problems, explanations and workings. Three chapters among the nine were especially valuable to carpentry: Field Measurement (area calculation), Reducing Dimensions (finding square and cube roots) and Construction Consultations (volume calculation). These three methods are widely used in wood product craftsmanship and have become the foundation of various techniques in later generations.
Desc_66.cn: 《九章》乃古代最早的算术之书，此书共有九章，收有二百四十六问，其中“方田”乃平面图形计算之法；“少广”乃开平方、开立方之法；“商功”乃计算立体体积之法，此三法均被普遍用于制木古法之中，为后世百工技艺的根基之一。

Desc_67.en: Lu Ban (507-444 BCE), a structural engineer during the Zhou Dynasty, was reputed to have once made a flying magpie from bamboo sticks that could fly in the sky for three days straight. Though mostly incomplete, Lu Ban's ideas are innovative without parallel, and compiled within this secret tome.
Desc_67.cn: “公输子削竹木以为鹊，成而飞之，三日不下”。《竹鹊志》乃是收录鲁班各种奇思妙想的奇书，书以竹鹊为名，内容前无古人，天马行空，可惜大多尚未完成。

Desc_68.en: One of the Ten Computational Canons, this book discusses astronomical observation and mathematical calculation. It's said Zhuge Liang (181-234 CE) of the Three Kingdoms period created his 'Wooden Bullocks and Horses' inventions by drawing inspiration from this work.
Desc_68.cn: 《周髀算经》一书囊括四季更替，气候变化之道、包涵南北有极，昼夜相推之理，为“算经十书”之一。相传，三国时期，诸葛卧龙阅《周髀算经》有感，遂造成木牛流马。

Desc_69.en: The author's identity unknown, he is referred to as the Great Artisan, and claimed to be an imperial palace architect during the Han Dynasty. This work records the building process of various palaces, temples and tombs, providing valuable information on ancient carpentry construction techniques used in that era.
Desc_69.cn: 此书乃是汉代一位不知其名的木匠所撰写，文中自叙其职为“将作大匠”，记载有其在职之时对于宫室、宗庙、陵寝土木营建之事，书中涵盖大量汉代木业建造之古法，对于后世研究制木法大有裨益，因其无名，后人便称此书为《大匠传》。

Desc_70.en: During the Qin Dynasty, Chancellor Li Si (280-208 BCE) ordered the construction of the Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang (259-210 BCE) and invited a renowned Mohist engineer to construct the contraptions within. Aware that this was to be his final job, he recorded all his experience and techniques mastered from a lifetime of creating mechanisms. As expected, the Emperor indeed had the entire workforce massacred upon the mausoleum's completion.
Desc_70.cn: 秦朝年间，丞相李斯奉命督造秦始皇陵，将当时一位德高望重的墨家老者请至建设皇陵机关，老者自知此去无回，遂将自己数十年研究机关造术之心血编撰成书后，入陵建造机关，皇陵建成之后，秦始皇下令尽杀百工，此书亦成老者绝书。

Desc_71.en: Compiled by generations of carpenters as a supplement to the Manual of Lu Ban, a structural engineering guide by a carpentry master. Highly regarded among carpenters for its detailed collection of thousands of woodworking techniques, spanning from palace buildings to daily utensils.
Desc_71.cn: 《公输记遗》乃后世木工根据祖师鲁班所书之《公输经》完善而成，书中记载有上千种制木之法，上至宫室营造，下至百姓用具，罗列百章，无不精深奥妙，为木工匠人奉为圭臬。

Desc_72.en: Compiled by Wang Xi of the Western Jin. This work provided a broad spectrum of discussions on pulse diagnosis, tracing the sources of hundreds of diseases, with examples, detailed symptoms, and various pulse shapes. A wondrous treatise on the 24 Pulses in traditional medicine.
Desc_72.cn: 《脉经》为西晋王熙所撰，书中总结了《内经》、《难经》等经论的要旨，融合了古代有关脉学及其多年行医的经验，乃是最早详细归纳了二十四种脉象的脉学专著。

Desc_73.en: Written by a physician named Chu Cheng in the Southern Qi Dynasty, this medical classic unravels the secrets of Qi and contains over ten insightful chapters, covering topics including Qi types, meridians, body fluids, organs, illnesses and their diagnosis, as well as some seminal ideas on reproductive medicine.
Desc_73.cn: 《褚氏遗书》为南齐褚澄所撰。书中分为受形、本气、平脉、津润、分体、精血、除疾、审微、辨书、问子十篇，乃是论述人体气血阴阳之奥妙的先驱，为后世医家奉为经典。

Desc_74.en: An ancient medical classic by Bian Que in the late Warring States period. Addresses 81 difficult medical conditions through a question-and-answer-style dialogue. Its expositions on meridians, organs and acupoints contained are discussed and referenced to this day.
Desc_74.cn: 《难经》乃是春秋战国晚期扁鹊所著，全书共分为八十一难，采用问答之方式论述医理，其中涵盖脉诊、经络、脏腑、阴阳、病因、病机、营卫、腧穴、针刺、病证十大门类，其中奇经八脉、三焦与命门之论述，均为后世医家所修习传承。

Desc_75.en: Written by a Tang Dynasty physician named Sun Simiao (?-682 BCE), this 30-volume classic lists circa 2,900 medicine recipes addressing 189 different medical conditions. It works as a supplement to another work created by Sun named 'Prescriptions Worth a Thousand Gold,' recording thirty years of Sun's own experience and epitomizing the very essence of pre-Tang Dynasty medicine.
Desc_75.cn: 《千金翼方》乃唐代孙思邈所著，全书共分三十卷，一百八十九门，两千九百余首，乃孙思邈集三十载行医经验，为补《千金要方》之不足著述而成，可谓一部淹贯众长，集医学大成之典籍。

Desc_76.en: Compiled by Zhang Zhongjing (150-219 CE) in the Eastern Han Dynasty. Consists of 12 volumes and a large number of compound formulas, precise and effective. These were honored as being the 'Progenitor of Formulas' and 'Classical Formulas' by later generations.
Desc_76.cn: 《伤寒论》成书于东汉，乃医圣张仲景所书，全书共十二卷，书上所载的大量复方，组方严谨，疗效显著，被后世誉为“众方之祖”，尊称为“经方”。

Desc_77.en: A work containing the knowledge and experience of Hua Tuo (145-208 CE). It is said that "Hua Tuo devoted his whole life to writing Green Bag Book." Consists of 32 chapters in 2 volumes, the first on medical theories and the second on surgery, a pioneer in the field. The surgical operations of "cutting open the chest and back, removing tumors, and lavaging the intestines" recorded in it were unimaginable at that time.
Desc_77.cn: “华佗倾毕生心血作青囊书”。《青囊书》全书共有两卷三十二章，上卷载药物理论之学说，下卷载外科手术之技法，其中记载的“刳剖腹背，抽割积聚，断肠滴洗”等一系列手术技法，皆可谓旷古绝学也。

Desc_78.en: A life-saving tome, composing the 'Miscellaneous Diseases' section of the Treatise on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Diseases by Zhang Zhongjing (150-219 CE) in the Eastern Han Dynasty. Consists of 25 chapters in 3 volumes, recording over 60 diseases and 262 formulas. One of the most important medicinal textbooks.
Desc_78.cn: “此书可以活人”。《金匮要略》乃东汉著名医学家张仲景所著《伤寒杂病论》之杂病部分，乃是一部论述杂病诊治之专书，全书分为三卷，共二十五篇，载疾病六十余种，收方剂二百六十二首，乃是医术中至关重要的典籍。

Desc_79.en: Reputedly authored by the Divine Farmer, second of China's mythical emperors. It took much time and effort of many during the Qin and Han dynasties to finish this book. Considered the essence of medical theory, it concisely records 365 herbal medicines' ingredients.
Desc_79.cn: 《神农本草经》源起神农氏，成书非一时，作者非一人，乃秦汉时期众多医者搜集，总结整理而出的草药学说，其中载药三百六十五种，文字简练古朴，可谓医药理论之精髓。

Desc_80.en: A work composed of two texts: Basic Questions and Spiritual Pivot. Based on Taoist theory, this secret tome gave birth to the Yin-yang and Five Elements, Pulse Condition, and Viscera-state theories thus laying the foundation for all these fields.
Desc_80.cn: 《黄帝内经》全书分为《灵枢》、《素问》两部分，于黄老道家理论之上建立“阴阳五行学说”、“脉象学说”、“藏象学说”等学说，内容丰富，包罗万象，其思想及理念决定了古今医学之走向与根基，乃始祖之典籍，旷世之奇书。

Desc_81.en: An introduction to various poisons, circulated around the Kingdom of Nanzhao during the Tang Dynasty. It describes the myriad symptoms caused by common lethal poisons, for instance, darkened complexion and rigor, bloating and festering, red eyes and internal bleeding, etc.
Desc_81.cn: 此书乃唐代南诏国一带所流传的毒物论本，书中记录了数十种常见毒物所引发的六种致死症状，如面黑僵死、全身肿溃、目赤呕血等，因而此书被时人称为《六害经》。

Desc_82.en: Composed of 25 chapters, this unprecedented classic records 347 types of poisonous herbs and their habitats, offering a detailed description of the toxic reaction and antidote for each.
Desc_82.cn: 《毒经》全书分为二十五篇，载有毒草药三百四十七门，详细写下了这些毒物的生长环境、误食后果及解毒方法，乃是古代第一部论述毒物之专著。

Desc_83.en: Written by Song Ci of the Song Dynasty. Contains 53 chapters in 5 volumes, covering 'Autopsy,' 'Bone Inspection,' 'Injury Inspection,' 'Medicine,' and 'Toxicology.' Extremely helpful in the study of poisoning and toxins.
Desc_83.cn: 《洗冤集录》成书于宋代，乃宋慈所著，全书有五卷，五十三条，写有验尸、验骨、验伤、中毒、救死方六大门类，其中除去“中毒”这一门类对研习毒术帮助极大之外，书中对各种伤、残、病、死之研究亦极大的加快了毒术研习之进境。

Desc_84.en: Written during the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms periods, the book was collected in the Bureau of Medicine by order of Emperor Taizu of the Song (927-976 CE). In around 2,000 characters, it records dozens of methods to make such poisons as Heartbreak Grass, Convulsion Extract and Zhen (extracted from a mythical bird), among which Convulsion Extract was used to kill Li Yu (937-978 CE), last ruler of the Southern Tang state. It is in the secret collection of the imperial family and forbidden among commoners.
Desc_84.cn: 《邪物论》成书于五代时期，为宋太祖赵匡胤收编于翰林医官院。此书共两千字，载“钩吻”、“牵机药”、“鸩毒”等数十种制毒方法，其中牵机药被赵匡胤用于赐死南唐后主李煜，此书乃皇家收藏之私书，民间不得流传。

Desc_85.en: Written by Fotudeng (232-348 CE), a Buddhist monk from Kucha, this book records all the rare toxicants that he discovered during his journey to Luoyang to spread Buddhism. Among the hundreds of poisons originating from 16 regions covered in the book, he destroyed 11 himself and abandoned 213 more for being too deadly. It was later mistaken as a work of fiction, due to the rarity of the toxicants within.
Desc_85.cn: 佛图澄为至中土弘教，自乌苌一路跋涉，途中将所遇之幽暗奇绝之毒物记录成册，册中涵盖其十六个地区的上百种毒物，其中佛图澄销毁了十一种，其余二百一十三类皆因其毒性奇烈而作罢，后此书传至洛阳，因其所载之毒物闻所未闻之故，被时人误为杜撰。

Desc_86.en: Written by an unknown elder from the Tang Dynasty, when drinking liquor was a pastime for both royal peers and hawkers alike. It details 39 kinds of drugs that are fatal when drunk with liquor. One drop means certain death, with no antidote.
Desc_86.cn: 唐朝年间，上至王公贵族，下至贩夫走卒，皆以饮酒为乐，当时有一位老者，录下三十九种入酒之药，借以酒之特性加强药物毒性，若饮此毒酒，一滴足以毙命，因其药性猛烈，无药可解，遂被称为《鬼壶经》。

Desc_87.en: Written on the 125 "low herbs" recorded in the "Herbal Classic of Divine Farmer" that have a strong or violent action on physiological functions and are often poisonous, the book only discussed the toxicity of these herbs but not the healing effect, so it was rarely known to the public in that era.
Desc_87.cn: “下药一百二十五种为佐使，主治病以应地，多毒，不可久服”。《本经下品注》乃是一本对于《神农百草经》中所载的一百二十五种“下药”之详细注解，注解者不论医药救人，只论“下药”之毒性，时人厌其不祥，故此书极少流传。

Desc_88.en: Written by the last disciple of Whitejade Toad (1134-1229 CE), the fifth master of the Southern Lineage of Taoism during the Song Dynasty. Describes 36 types of toxicants corresponding to the 36 acupoint weaknesses of the body that can damage pressure points and disrupt one's meridian system. Considered a collection of deadly toxicants, for they have no known cure.
Desc_88.cn: 《百损经》乃宋代道教南五祖之一白玉蟾关门弟子所书，书中载录三十六类毒药，分别对应人体三十六死穴，损穴毁脉无补救之法，故而此经书所载之毒并无解药，因其霸道之特性，为时人谓之杀手。

Desc_89.en: Written by a peculiar physician in the Song Dynasty (960-1279 CE). Consists of 5 chapters: Miasma, Minerals, Water, Plants, and Insects. With 1,236 toxins recorded within, it's the most comprehensive poison tome in history. Named as such due to the emerald robes favored by the author.
Desc_89.cn: 《青衣密要》乃宋代一位怪医所著，全书共分作瘴，矿，水，草，虫五章，罗列天下有毒之物共计一千二百三十六条，乃是古往今来，记载毒物最为俱全之书，因此怪医生平只着青衣，故称此书为《青衣密要》。

Desc_90.en: Written by an unknown weaver woman from the Song Dynasty (960-1279 CE). The book covers all known procedures for crafting silk gauze. Its prose plain and simple, it soon became essential introductory reading for all weavers.
Desc_90.cn: 《花罗谱》乃宋代一位无名织女所著，此书中记叙了罗的制成之法，详细记载了挑丝、泡丝、捻丝、打绘、穿综、绘版至上机织造等近三十道工序，文字简朴无华，浅显易懂，乃是织造匠人入门之读物。

Desc_91.en: The Li people are known for their exquisite weaving skills. During the Song Dynasty (960-1279 CE), the author of this book visited Hainan. He lived among the Li natives for twelve years, during which he wrote this work. It consists of 3 chapters: embroidering, dyeing and printing, giving great detail on the Li's tapestries.
Desc_91.cn: “黎人善织锦，制作精巧，色彩绮丽”。宋代有汉人至海南岛，住一十二载，写著《黎人古语》一书，全书共分为织绣、织染、织花三章，详细记载了黎锦的制成方法以及制作技巧，为时人所习。

Desc_92.en: Originally a key text of the official Dyeing Division in the Qin Dynasty (221-207 BCE), it records the dyeing procedures of 39 different colors. This division was disbanded when the Dynasty fell, its personnel scattered and this work lost. Years later, its contents were compiled into this book.
Desc_92.cn: 秦朝染色司记其练染法作为司内传阅之物，笔记中详细论述三十九种色彩之练染方法，后秦朝覆灭，染色司众人逃散，此笔记流落民间，为后人编订成书，命名为《练染集注》。

Desc_93.en: In the Han Dynasty tradition, the empress would attend to the mulberry trees personally to make offerings to the goddess of the silkworms. During the Western Han Dynasty, Empress Dou held a rite of sericulture (silk production) and ordered this book's compilation, in which all ancient weaving skills are recorded.
Desc_93.cn: “汉仪，皇后亲桑东郊苑中，蚕室祭蚕神，曰苑窊妇人、寓氏公主祠。”西汉年间，窦皇后举行先蚕祀，并命织室匠人编造《桑蚕经》，将秦汉两代织造技艺古法记录在册，广传民间。

Desc_94.en: Written by a nameless author in Chang'an, in the Tang Dynasty (618-907 CE). With witty and flowing prose it describes the clothing of Tang commoners with rich illustrations, and is a treasure trove of information on the period.
Desc_94.cn: 唐代长安一位无名人士根据时下所流传的一则《借衣买酒》的怪奇故事，撰写出《借衣记》一书，书中以诙谐言语描写由唐一代平民百姓日常服饰以及穿着，并附图画讲解，乃是集唐代服饰之大全者。

Desc_95.en: A wide tapestry from the Song Dynasty bearing the seal of artist Zhu Kerou. An elegant piece portraying a family of ducks leisurely swimming in a lotus pond, surrounded by flowers and other birds that are equally lifelike.
Desc_95.cn: 《莲塘乳鸭图》荷花造型丰满，白色瓣尖染红，白鹭鸟神情精灵剔透，一雌一雄双鸭游哉悠哉，身旁伴一双儿女活泼纯真，可爱稚拙，画面生动温馨，色彩变化丰富，缂丝组织细密，丝丝缕缕匀称分明，乃是上乘之作。

Desc_96.en: One of the Thirteen Confucian Classics. The book details the rites, ceremonies, protocols, and social customs of the Zhou Dynasty. Designs and information for all kinds of official ritual wear are also found within, making it a key tailoring text.
Desc_96.cn: 《仪礼》为儒家十三经之一，全书共十七篇，乃是根据春秋战国时期之礼制汇编而成，书中载录的春秋战国时期周天子乃至卿大夫十七类典制所着之衣裳，乃是织造业织造官服之圭臬。

Desc_97.en: Complied in 705 CE, this book recorded all weaving patterns known from the Shang to the Tang Dynasty, and their significance. With abundant descriptions and beautiful writing, it's regarded as among the best records on the topic in history.
Desc_97.cn: 《百花锦册》成书于唐代神龙元年，书中记载自商周至大唐年间的服饰花纹样式及内在含义，其叙述详尽，辞藻瑰丽，可谓古今往来记花锦之绝书也。

Desc_98.en: Lei Zu was titled 'The Progenitor of Silk,' deemed to have invented the silk extraction and weaving processes. From the Xia Dynasty (2070-1600 BCE) onward, generations of craftsmen have devoted themselves to collecting these ancient methods, and so the book was finally finished in the Han Dynasty. Crystallizing centuries of hard graft, this tome is truly invaluable.
Desc_98.cn: 嫘祖发明养蚕缫丝之法，被世人称为“蚕祖”。自夏朝始，历代织造名匠便倾毕生之力收集嫘祖养蚕缫丝古法，终至汉朝年间方成《先蚕嫘祖记》，可谓经百载时光而心血不断，倾千人之力作绝世之书。

Desc_99.en: Prized by jade traders during the Song Dynasty (960-1279 CE). It includes the sources and properties of jade-polishing powders from lands the world over. It's the most comprehensive record of its kind.
Desc_99.cn: 《解玉》乃是宋朝年间玉石行业内所收藏之书籍，此书收录了宋朝各地所出产的解玉砂的性质及其形态，是有宋一代记载解玉砂最为完全者。

Desc_100.en: A masterpiece painting presented by Jiang Ziya to King Wu of Zhou, depicting six types of jadeware. Having established the Zhou Dynasty, the king would later use them in rituals and when appointing officials, hence this piece's name.
Desc_100.cn: 相传《六瑞图》乃姜子牙献周武王之宝图，其上绘镇圭，桓圭，信圭，躬圭，谷璧，蒲璧六类玉器，后周武王建立周朝，将此六类玉器用于官员之朝聘，并命此六器为“六瑞”。

Desc_101.en: Among the royal collections of the Song Dynasty (960-1279 CE), this book records seven ancient jadeworking procedures within its four chapters. It was essential reading for all jadeworkers of the time.
Desc_101.cn: 《琢玉录》乃是宋代时皇家收录的藏书，全书共分为相玉，划活，琢磨 ，碾磨四章，书中载录了双钩碾法，金错玉器，软玉法，软晶法等七种碾玉古法，乃琢玉匠人不可不读之书。

Desc_102.en: A 2-volume gemology classic split between jade and stone, written in the late Tang Dynasty, author unknown. Details 16 types of jades, as well as the regions in which they are produced. These books are difficult to come by and are highly valued by jewelers far and wide.
Desc_102.cn: 《八珍八宝记》成书于唐代晚期，作者姓名不详，全书共分上下两卷，上卷载玉，下卷载石，全书收录了壁流离，吠琉璃，绿松石，碧玉，瑾瑜，金精，金星石等十六类玉石种类及其出产之地，乃是玉石行业业内所传阅之读物，不可多得。

Desc_103.en: Meng Chang (919-965 CE) was the ruler of the later Shu kingdom and extremely fond of Lady Huarui, one of his concubines. He likened her skin to smooth ice, and her bones to jade; praised her as possessing a heavenly beauty, upon whom only celestial gemstones and jades were fit to be worn. And so he spent a tremendous amount of his wealth upon 36 kinds of gemstones, each brimming with a different brilliance when worn by his love. In awe, Meng Chang then composed the 36 poems and essays found in this book.
Desc_103.cn: 后蜀主孟昶极为宠爱花蕊夫人，言她冰肌玉骨柔媚天成，认为只有仙界玉石方能衬其容貌，于是花费万金求购得三十六类宝石，其所溢辉光皆有所不同，花蕊夫人每每佩戴亦有所异，孟昶有感，遂著诗文共计三十六篇，命其为《石华说》。

Desc_104.en: It is said that upon the death of Li Chun, an artisan of the Sui Dynasty (581-619 CE), he was buried beside the Anji Bridge he'd designed. Grass and flowers bloomed upon his grave, despite it being the middle of winter. Upon closer inspection, people found numerous treasures lying about his grave. Amazed by these peculiar occurrences, the treasures were recorded within this book.
Desc_104.cn: 相传隋朝匠师李春逝世后，被葬于赵州桥旁，时年冬月，百草枯亡，唯有李春墓地草长莺飞，有人前往探查，见其墓地出现数百种金石玉器，时人以为奇，遂将此墓所出之珠宝记录在册，命其为《异魂志》。

Desc_105.en: Few tools were used in jadeworking during the Southern and Northern Dynasties (420-589 CE). It was low-efficiency work that yielded a poor-quality product. That is, until a young man invented the grinding wheel and four jadeworking techniques that made it feasible. These were later compiled into this book.
Desc_105.cn: “砣，琢玉之具也”。魏晋南北朝年间琢玉工具唯有线材及弓子，打磨玉石极为耗力且玉品不佳，时年间出现了一位极善琢玉的少年，他以圆盘造砣，并发明出扎砣，冲砣，磨砣，掏堂四种琢玉之法，后有人将此四法编撰成书，取名为《宝砣经》。

Desc_106.en: In ancient times, there was an immortal named Yi Xiang. He had no supernatural power, but was skilled at cultivating jade. He would wander the mortal realms, passing his knowledge of jade on to those he liked. A magnate in the Han Dynasty, also keen on jade, collected the quotations of Yi Xiang and compiled them into this book.
Desc_106.cn: 上古之时，有位名叫以向的神人，无甚法力，却善养玉，犹爱浪荡人间，若遇有缘人则传授养玉之法门。汉朝有一位善于养玉的富商，收集以向养玉的言论编撰成书，取名为《以向养玉经》。

Desc_107.en: There was once a young, handsome nobleman called Liu Hua during the Five Dynasties period. It's said that, whilst napping in the garden one day, the goddess Queen Mother of the West happened across him. She took him up into the heavens, where they spent many a day together. Upon his eventual departure she gifted him with celestial jewelry. Awakening, he believed it a dream; but knew it to be real when he saw the jewelry. His experience is recorded in this story.
Desc_107.cn: 五代年间，后蜀士族中有位叫刘华的少年，其姿容绮丽，跌宕风流，相传他一日园中小憩，忽梦霞光葳蕤，西王母乘云雾而至，邀刘华一游昆仑仙宫，缠绵多时，临别之际西王母将仙宫珠宝相赠，刘华惊醒之后，果真见榻前珍奇堆积，后此事为时人记载成书，谓其《瑶池游记》。

Desc_108.en: Written by Laozi in the Spring & Autumn period and compiled by Wei Huacun (251-334 CE), one of the founders of the Shangqing School tradition. Based on Taoist and traditional medicine theories, the book covers Meditation, Life Cultivation, and Internal Alchemy as means to achieve immortality. It was studied extensively among the Eastern Jin Dynasty's literary spheres.
Desc_108.cn: 《黄庭经》乃春秋战国时期李耳所著，由天师道魏华存自创门户而普传于世，全书以道教思神守一，宝精爱气之说与古代医家脏腑理论相结合，述其修炼长生成仙之术，为东晋士大夫阶层广泛修习。

Desc_109.en: A work also known by the longer title of The Perfect Classic of the Beginning of the Scripture of the Supreme Wonderful Way. Enlightened by Laozi, Yin Xi (aka. Guanyinzi, lit. 'Master Yin of the Pass') embraced the Supreme Way and wrote this book. It's praised as profound and meaningful, and said to be the subtlest of the Taoist canon.
Desc_109.cn: 关尹子受老子教诲，开发其智，修证大道，遂成《文始真经》。此书文辞沈博绝丽，意境深远隽永，故而时人谓之：道家大藏千万卷，最精微者关尹子书也。

Desc_110.en: The Huainanzi was written by Liu An (179-122 BCE), Prince of Huainan, and his court scholars. Based on Taoist doctrines, this book blends other schools' concepts with romantic and fantastic texts and was highly respected by later scholars.
Desc_110.cn: 《淮南子》乃淮南王刘安及其幕下士人撰写而成，此书以黄老学说为主题思想，融会诸子百家之言，其文浪漫诡奇，为后学所崇。

Desc_111.en: Written by Ge Hong (285-343 CE) of the Jin Dynasty. Divided into the 'Inner Chapters' and the 'Outer Chapters' (on techniques to achieve immortality, and politics and society, respectively). The text presents the ethos of the Wei and Jin periods, earning it a place in Taoist literature.
Desc_111.cn: 《抱朴子》乃晋代葛洪所著，全书共八卷，内篇二十篇言神仙吐纳符篆勉治之术；外篇五十篇言时政得失，人事臧否，文呈魏晋飘渺之风骨，占道家文籍一席之地。

Desc_112.en: Written by Wenzi of the Song kingdom during the Spring and Autumn (770-476 BCE) and Warring States (476-221 BCE) periods. Utilizes other contemporary schools' concepts as a means to approach Taoist thought, combining the essences of different ideologies.
Desc_112.cn: 此经书成于春秋战国时期，乃宋国人士计然所著，书中以名、法、儒、墨诸家之言述其道家思想，旨博奥而辞文真，可谓萃万古为一编，诚经世之枢要。

Desc_113.en: Written by Liezi who was given the title 'The Simple and Vacuous One' (a respectful title) by Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang Dynasty. As one of the four Taoist classics, eight of its chapters remain today, each eloquently expounding different aspects of the author's ideas.
Desc_113.cn: 天宝年间唐玄宗诏封列子为“冲虚真人”，命其所著真经为《冲虚真经》，此经书乃道教四部圣典之一，现行八篇，每篇皆以语言叙述其思想，内容驳杂，书事简劲宏妙，气伟而采奇。

Desc_114.en: Compiled by Zhuangzi (359-286 BCE) and his students in the Warring States period, this title (known also simply as the Zhuangzi) along with the Book of Changes and the Classic of the Way and Virtue were called the 'Three Mysterious Works.' Its vast content matter includes philosophy, life, politics, society, arts, and the cosmos.
Desc_114.cn: 《南华真经》乃春秋战国时期庄子及其后学所著，与《老子》《周易》并称三玄。此书包罗万象，对其哲学、人生、政治、社会、艺术、宇宙皆有详细论述，被誉为：“钳揵九流，括囊百氏”。

Desc_115.en: The hidden represents the unseen, and Talisman represents the unchangeable Tao that has been inherited.' Classic of Secret Revelation is a Taoist canon that allegedly "provides clues to the unseen." It is said to have been written during the Yellow Emperor's reign, with around 400 words in total. In a terse but comprehensive style, it contains the profound truth of the universe and is deemed one of the greatest Taoist classics.
Desc_115.cn: “隐微难见，故名为阴；妙合大道，名之为符。经者，万古之常法也。”《黄帝阴符经》相传书成于轩辕黄帝时期，全书共四百余字，其说理透彻、言简意赅，内容精微深奥，乃道家经典，被誉为“道家双壁”之一。

Desc_116.en: Laozi once lived in the Captal of Zhou, but eventually left during its decline. Upon leaving the final pass, Yin Xi stopped him, saying "O Master, I see that you are leaving, but please enlighten me with your wisdom and write a book for me before you leave." So Laozi wrote a book of 5,000 words that became known as Tao Te Ching. The book comprised two parts, The Way and Virtue. It covered the topics of morality, politics, military, and life. It's highly esteemed by later generations and entitled the King of Classics.
Desc_116.cn: “老子居周久之，见周之衰，乃遂去。至关，关尹喜曰：子将隐矣，强为我著书，于是老子言道德五千言而去，遂成《道德经》。”《道德经》全书共分为上下两篇，以“道德”为纲宗，论述修身、治国、用兵、养生之道，此书为后世所崇仰，被奉为万经之王。

Desc_117.en: Part of the Large Perfection of Wisdom Sutra, it condenses the essence of Great Prajnaparamita within a mere 260 or so characters; the heart of wisdom, hence its name. It may be brief, but its meanings are profound.
Desc_117.cn: 此经书全文只二百六十字，属六百部般若之一卷，般若之经意皆设于此经，乃《大般若经》心髓，故而谓之《心经》，此经书言简而义丰， 词寡而旨深。

Desc_118.en: Compiled in ancient India. It records a discussion on Sutra between Buddha and Subhūti and other disciples. It's a classic that illustrates the enlightening insight of the Buddha.
Desc_118.cn: 《金刚经》成书于古印度，书中记述佛陀弟子阿傩记载如来世尊释迦牟尼在世时与长老须菩提等众弟子谈论佛经的经过，是一部阐扬佛性密意的经典之作。

Desc_119.en: Translated by Siksananda (652-710 CE), an eminent monk in the Tang Dynasty, this Sutra tells of how Ksitigarbha became a bodhisattva by vowing to rescue all condemned sentient beings, with a description of his filial piety in past lifetimes. Easy to understand, it proved popular among commoners.
Desc_119.cn: 唐朝高僧实叉难陀译《地藏经》，本经叙说地藏菩萨之本愿功德，及本生之誓愿，强调地藏菩萨不可思议之大愿力，因此经书浅显易懂，故广受时人追捧。

Desc_120.en: During the reign of the Emperor Ming of Han (58-75 CE), two Indian monks Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna were brought to Luoyang and built White Steed Temple, where they translated this Sutra. It contains 42 quotations from Buddha, covering the Mahayana and Hinayana doctrines and various teachings. It is thus known as one of the Three Sutras of the Buddha's Direct Teachings.
Desc_120.cn: 永平十年，使者携摄摩腾和竺法兰返国，于雒阳立白马寺，译出《四十二章经》。此书载录佛陀四十二段语录，通摄大小乘一切教义，涵诸法要，被尊为“佛遗教三经”之一。

Desc_121.en: The Infinite Life Sutra concerns Amitabha's vows made to save all sentient beings, while the Contemplation Sutra tells of the 16 contemplations that enable one's rebirth into the Pure Land and the nine levels of those born therein. Lastly, the Amitabha Sutra details the wondrous adornments awaiting the righteous in the Western Pure Land and the beings that reside there, including the Amitabha Buddha. These three sutras are the fundamental classics of the Pure Land Sect of Han Dynasty.
Desc_121.cn: 《净土三经》中《无量寿经》宣说其阿弥陀佛接引众生之大愿；《观经》宣说其观想念佛的十六次第 ，净业三福，及九品往生；《阿弥陀经》宣说其极乐世界的庄严以及阿弥陀佛佛号的由来与意义，劝众生发愿往生极乐世界，此三经乃汉传净土宗之根本经典。

Desc_122.en: The Dirgha Agama (lit. 'Long Discourses') is an agama, a collection of Early Buddhist scriptures, containing longer chapters. Foundational to Buddhism, it contains the Buddha's early teachings and quotations within a concise yet profound script.
Desc_122.cn: 《长阿含经》为“四阿含”之一，因所集各经篇幅较长，说久远事，故称“长阿含”，此经记录佛陀之开示录、言行录，其行文简炼，意趣深远，乃是佛法的根本，佛世流传之“教法”。

Desc_123.en: A compilation of disparate texts on various topics such as the Bodhisattva path, the interpenetration of phenomena (dharmas), the visionary powers of meditation, and the equality of things in emptiness. Regarded as the mightiest of the classic tomes by many Mahayana schools of thought.
Desc_123.cn: 《华严经》据称乃释迦牟尼佛成道后，在禅定中解释无尽法界时所宣讲，以因果缘起理实法界为宗，说菩萨以菩提心为因而修诸行，顿入佛地之因果，被大乘诸宗奉为“万经之王。”

Desc_124.en: One of The Threefold Lotus Sutras. It contains the Shakyamuni Buddha's later teachings and is arguably the most famous of all Buddhist texts, presenting both the Buddhist path and the Buddha himself.
Desc_124.cn: 《妙法莲华经》乃法华三部经之一，为佛陀释迦牟尼晚年所说之教法，以“声闻”、“独觉”二乘为权说，开启了“回小向大”的门径，此言于佛教思想史上占有至关重要之地位。

Desc_125.en: Reading the Surangama Sutra strips all other written works of their meaning! First translated by the mystical Buddhist Pramiti in the first year after Emperor Zhongzong of Tang relinquished his throne (705 C. E.), the Buddhist scripture encompasses every important theory of Mahayana with extensive exposition and close reasoning, thus extolled as a Mahayana classic.
Desc_125.cn: “自从一读楞严后，不看人间糟粕书！”。般剌密谛于唐中宗神龙元年译出《楞严经》，此经书内容宏富，思想严密，将所有大乘佛教重要理论皆囊括其中，可谓大乘佛教之经典。

Desc_126.en: Written by a Song Dynasty (960-1279 CE) cook. It contains 37 individual recipes, all using common ingredients and easy to follow. Named as such owing to its recipes for foods catering to the four major classes of the time: The scholar-officials, farmers, artisans and merchants.
Desc_126.cn: 此书乃是宋朝年间松江府的一位庖丁所书，书中所载三十七道菜肴制作方法，皆取平民百姓常见之菜类，做法简便易学，因囊括士农工商四民日常所食，故而时人将其谓之《四民食录》。

Desc_127.en: In 1179 CE, Emperor Gaozong of the Song Dynasty Zhao Gou visited the West Lake. He ordered his servants to buy turtles and fish, and then set them free for good karma. Among them was Song Wusao, a lady who claimed to have lived in the former capital, fleeing here with the Emperor, and cooked fish broth for a living. The Emperor summoned her, sampled her broth and found it to his liking. She was thus rewarded with treasure and widespread fame.
Desc_127.cn: 淳熙六年，宋高宗赵构乘御舟游西湖，命内侍买龟、鱼放生，宣唤中有一卖鱼羹的妇人叫宋五嫂，自称开封人氏，随皇上南迁至此，于西湖制鱼羹为生，高宗命其上船，尝其鱼羹，大赞，赏锦帛金银，从此宋五嫂声名鹊起，于是时有《宋嫂食单》。

Desc_128.en: Written by an old man named Benxin and compiled by his disciple Chen Dasou. The book contains 20 vegetarian dishes, each described by a short poem. The words of the poems were clear and elegant, the sentiment graceful and ethereal.
Desc_128.cn: 《本心斋食谱》乃一位名唤本心的老者所写，门人陈达叟为其编辑，书中谱述二十品素食，写以十六字赞词，其词舂容大雅，不染浊气，其情雅量高致，幽静出尘。

Desc_129.en: Written by the agricultural pioneer Fan Sheng in the Han Dynasty (206 BCE-220 CE), this text draws upon pre-Qin (before 221 BCE) literature and his own experience and is the foundation of Chinese agronomy. It expands upon the cultivation techniques of 13 crops including grain, millet, wheat and rice.
Desc_129.cn: 西汉末年，农学家氾胜之根据先秦诸书以及自身经验著述出《氾胜之书》，书中载录了禾，黍，麦，稻，稗等十三类农作物栽培之技术，乃后世农学之源流。

Desc_130.en: While time marches ever forward and memories fade like dreams, the only proof that the golden ages of old existed is these 58 dishes. Written by a Tang Dynasty chancellor, Wei Juyuan (631-710 CE), this menu's dishes are all from the Tail-Burning Banquet that he prepared for Emperor Zhong Zong. The banquet was extremely luxurious, and lauded for generations.
Desc_130.cn: “鸡鸣枕上，夜气方回，百年承平，皆成梦中，唯此五十八食，证盛世曾存。”《烧尾食单》一书乃长安杜陵人氏韦巨源所著，书中载录了景龙二年韦巨源为敬奉中宗而举办的烧尾宴食单，其上录有五十八种菜点名称，其菜品之精美，用料之奢侈，为后人所叹。

Desc_131.en: Written by Lin Hong (1137-1162 CE) of the Song Dynasty. Records a variety of fruits, vegetables, birds and beasts and how they may be cooked. Filled with quotations and poetry galore, it's a clear and beautiful text.
Desc_131.cn: 《山家清供》乃宋代林洪所著，全书广收博采，载田野果蔬，山林奇珍，农家家禽，记其名，叙其用料，述其烹饪之法，行文间涉其典故诗文，用词清丽。

Desc_132.en: Written by Cui Hao (381-450 CE) of the Northern Wei Dynasty. Details the cooking and preservation of various foods, as dictated by his mother and other female family members. It's an elegant piece of writing that embodies Northern Wei culinary culture.
Desc_132.cn: 《食经》乃北魏崔浩所书，书有九卷，言多种食物储藏及肴馔制作，乃崔母卢氏与族中妇人口授，崔浩记之，文辞约举，婉而成章，囊括北魏一代饮食文化之大成。

Desc_133.en: Written by Jia Sixie of the Northern Wei Dynasty (386-534 CE). In 10 volumes and 92 chapters it discusses agriculture, horticulture, forestry, fishing, veterinary medicine, breeding, brewing, cooking, and storage among others. A commoner family in the Tang Dynasty preserved fruits with honey as instructed by this work, and the results were so successful that it actually gained royal approval.
Desc_133.cn: 《齐民要术》乃农学家贾思勰所著。书分十卷九十二篇，概述其农、林、牧、渔、副等手工业生产及食物贮藏知识，唐朝年间，资州内江县一户刘氏人家根据《齐民要术》贮藏食物一篇，将金钱桔 、梨脯、杏子、寿星桔、等水果以蜂蜜浸泡储存，此法保糖保汁，其味香甜可口，后为皇家列为贡果。

Desc_134.en: Written by Yu Cong (435-499 CE) of the Southern Qi Dynasty. Contains dishes from Jiangnan, ancient recipes combined with his own personal innovation. Considered to include some of the best recipes of all time, the Book of the Southern Qi states that "Cong excels in cuisine, both his cookery and flavoring utterly unique."
Desc_134.cn: 南齐时代，余姚虞氏虞悰著述《食珍录》一书，书中主要记载江南风味之菜肴，其烹饪之法乃虞悰自身独创配以前人古法，为其一绝，于六朝饮食珍谱拔得头筹，《南齐书》称“悰善为滋味，和齐皆有方法”。

Desc_135.en: A collection of Su Shi's (1037-1101 CE) essays. Whether long or short, all were written in a free and natural way, with an elegance and inspiring manner found throughout all his works.
Desc_135.cn: 元丰年间苏轼写杂说史论总编为《东坡志林》，其文长短不拘，皆信笔写来，挥洒自如，行云流水涉笔成趣，乃其真风流也。

Desc_136.en: Written by Tao Gu (903-970 CE) of the Song Dynasty. Consists of 37 sections, covering fields from astronomy and politics to pets and furniture, and even branching out to deities and ghosts. It seems to cover almost everything and is a fascinating read.
Desc_136.cn: 宋代陶谷著述《清异录》一书，全书多摘采隽语异闻，凡分门三十有九，上载天文地理、人事官志、草木花果、虫鱼鸟兽、居室器用乃至仙神鬼妖，无所不备，读之趣味甚浓。

Desc_137.en: Compiled by Wu Ping of the Eastern Han Dynasty (25-220 CE), this book mainly concerns the states of Wu and Yue during the Spring and Autumn Period, as well as some information on other states of the time. It's often regarded as the first local historical chronicle.
Desc_137.cn: 《越绝书》乃东汉吴平所撰，主述春秋吴、越两国之稗官野史，旁及诸侯列国，乃后世历史小说之滥觞，又被誉为“地方志之鼻祖”。

Desc_138.en: Compiled either during the Warring States period (476-221 BCE) or the Han Dynasty (202 BCE-220 CE), author unknown. It's a 19-chapter dictionary progenitor that spans over 4,300 words, and was officially categorized as one of the Thirteen Confucian Classics.
Desc_138.cn: 《尔雅》成书于战国或两汉之间，书有十九篇，收录词语四千三百余，乃“辞书之祖”，后世儒家将其列入十三经中，奉为“儒家经典”。

Desc_139.en: So delightful it is to see the mountains and seas, and then the whole universe. Compiled pre-Qin Dynasty (up to 221 BCE), this hefty and magnificent tome is a collection of Chinese mythology. Within its pages one can find strange and wonderful tales and theories, discussions of fantastic lands, secret dwellings, and all that lies within. 18 extant chapters remain from the original 22.
Desc_139.cn: “观其山海，俯仰宇宙，得其乐也”。《山海经》乃先秦古籍，书原二十有二篇目，现存十八篇，上载怪奇悠谬之说，荟萃珍奇博物之地理，其用笔汪洋恣意，思想瑰丽奇幻。

Desc_140.en: A work penned by Wang Chan, who is also named Guiguzi, during the Warring States (476-221 BCE) period. In its 23 chapters, it features the arts of diplomacy and the trickery of politics, solidifying the School of Diplomacy's position in the Warring States period.
Desc_140.cn: 春秋战国时期纵横家鼻祖王禅著述《鬼谷子》一书，全书总有二十三篇目，书其纵横捭阖，言其谋略权术，王禅以此书定纵横家之地位，也定春秋之乱世。

Desc_141.en: Compiled by Liu Xiang and his son Liu Xin in the Han Dynasty. Divided into 7 sections and 38 categories, it was the first monumental and comprehensive bibliographical work in the history of China. It describes the flourishing of all kinds of academics from the pre-Qin to the Western Han Dynasties and discusses the authenticity of the collection of books and scriptures of the time. It is known as the academic and cultural history of the Western Han Dynasty.
Desc_141.cn: 《七略》乃汉代刘向所著，书以七略三十八类之分类法，条分缕析先秦至西汉的各种文化学术流派；以辑略之形式，于整体上评述各类文化学术的兴衰分合；以各书叙录，具体而微地介绍各种学术文化著作的优劣真伪是非，可谓其为西汉一代之学术文化史。

Desc_142.en: Compiled by Mozi (468-376 BCE) and his disciples, this tome expounds the Mohist philosophy. It propounds Mohist ideas such as impartiality, meritocratic governance, economic growth and aversion to ostentatiosness, and is known for its plain and simple language.
Desc_142.cn: 《墨子》书共五十三篇，乃墨子与各代门徒逐渐增补而成，书中记载墨家认识论与逻辑思想，其中墨辩独具一格，可谓先秦逻辑思想史的奠基之作。

Desc_143.en: Written by Shen Kuo (1031-1095 BCE) of the Song Dynasty after his retirement. Divided into 17 sections, it's an all-inclusive work covering numerous topics from politics to rumors, natural science to historical phenomena.
Desc_143.cn: 宋朝年间，沈括晚年归退后于润州卜居处著述出《梦溪笔谈》一书，全书共分十七门，涉及内容广博，上达官员权智，下至闾巷之言，又涉及古代自然科学、工艺技术及其社会历史现象，其囊括万千，无所不通。
